# Implementation Plan: Copilot Read-Only Submodule Snapshot Fast Path
<!-- ralph-meta {"overviewTaskId":"ralph-copilot-exec-readonly-submodule-snapshot-cost"} -->

*Generated by `/plan-with-ralph` on 2026-06-13. Ready for `/implement-with-ralph --from-plan D:\harness-efforts\codexu\.ralph\jobs\ralph-copilot-exec-readonly-submodule-snapshot-cost\plan.md`.*

## Overview
Re-enable Ralph's Copilot read-only snapshot/revert guard by replacing the nested-repo byte-manifest path with a per-nested-repo git fast-path. Initialized submodules under the cwd should be protected with the same shape the parent tree already uses: tracked/index/status metadata from that repo's own git database, clean tracked files restored from HEAD/index blobs, and byte capture only for pre-existing dirty or untracked content that cannot be reconstructed from git.

The plan deliberately preserves whole-cwd protection for every initialized nested repo, including submodules outside the plugin edit zone. It rejects policy-skipping large submodules as a regression, adds a fail-closed resource budget that aborts before launching the Copilot child, and keeps the implementation in the `ai-developer-toolkit` submodule's `plugins/ralph` plugin. The codexu wrapper pointer/table update remains a lead-owned submodule ship ceremony after implementation lands.

## Research Findings
### Codebase Context
- Seeded from brainstorm: `D:\harness-efforts\codexu\.ralph\brainstorms\ralph-copilot-exec-readonly-submodule-snapshot-cost\selected-direction.md`.
- `plugins/ralph/src/worktree-snapshot.mjs` owns the reusable guard primitive. The parent git path already records tracked files, exact index entries, and dirty/untracked content without byte-reading every clean file.
- `captureManifest()` is the current expensive nested-repo fallback: it walks a nested repo and `readFileSync`s every file into the snapshot. That is the memory blowup when codexu has initialized `codex/` and `ai-developer-toolkit/` submodules.
- `findNestedRepoRoots()` currently discovers `.git` boundaries through a broad DFS and does not stop descending at nested roots. It should return each initialized nested repo once and avoid nested-within-nested double work.
- `plugins/ralph/src/copilot-exec.mjs` currently has `READONLY_SNAPSHOT_ENABLED = false`; read-only mode still passes `--deny-tool=write`, but it does not revert shell-based writes until the snapshot path is safe again.
- Existing tests cover parent-tree clean/dirty/untracked/partial-staging behavior and one simple nested repo manifest case. They do not cover initialized submodule index fidelity, budget aborts, or no-whole-tree byte capture.

### Technical Constraints
- Whole-cwd protection must remain: every initialized nested repo under cwd is in scope, not only `ai-developer-toolkit/`.
- Gitignored files inside initialized nested repos are out of scope for the restored guarantee. This is already documented for the parent git-visible contract and must be explicit in comments/tests because the old manifest path accidentally covered ignored files.
- Exact restore fidelity requires nested repo index replay, not just worktree byte writes. The nested path must preserve clean, dirty-unstaged, staged, partially-staged, staged deletion, rename, and mode-bit states.
- Exact restore fidelity also requires detecting index-only and mode-only mutations. A model can corrupt staging without changing worktree bytes, so post-run index entries must be compared to pre-run entries independently of `contentsDiffer()`.
- Dirty/untracked bytes that do not exist in the object database must be captured or spilled before the child runs; clean tracked bytes should never be held in heap. Large dirty/untracked captures must be streamed/spilled only after budget reservation.
- The resource budget must fail closed before child launch with a distinct diagnostic and no partial snapshot. It must not silently skip the remainder of a large tree.
- Ralph plugin releases require synchronized version stamps across three plugin manifests and three marketplace indexes.

## Approach
### Architecture
Add a nested git snapshot representation that mirrors the existing parent snapshot fields per nested repo: `root`, `rootRel`, `trackedFiles`, `indexEntries`, `captured`, `preExistingDirs`, and `headExists`. Use the nested repo's own `git ls-files -z`, `git ls-files --stage -z`, and `git status --porcelain=v1 -z -uall` output. Clean tracked files are represented by git object identity and restored from `HEAD:<path>` or `:<path>`; only dirty/untracked/deleted pre-run candidates store content metadata.

Nested discovery must build a complete initialized-repo forest, not a flat "first boundary wins" list. A parent repo snapshot can stop file walking at a child `.git` boundary, but discovery still needs to find initialized repos at any depth, including `parent -> codex-like submodule -> initialized child submodule`. Capture each repo root exactly once, sort/relate parent-child roots, and make parent nested snapshots skip child repo roots while child snapshots protect their own contents. This preserves whole-cwd protection without double-capturing nested-within-nested repos.

Refactor the current parent helpers just enough to reuse them with an arbitrary repo root and display root. Avoid a large abstraction rewrite: preserve the parent-tree behavior, then introduce a small nested-git path that can share parsing, `preRunContent`, `restoreFile`, `restoreIndexEntry`, and candidate selection.

Resource-budget accounting should live in `captureSnapshot()` and be passed into nested capture. Track `capturedBytes` and `capturedFiles` for dirty/untracked byte captures and spill files. Budgeting must be stat-first: `lstat` the candidate, reserve file-count/byte budget, and only then read or stream-copy the content. Large or binary captured content should spill to a temp directory outside the protected cwd without materializing a whole Buffer. When limits are exceeded, throw a dedicated error type such as `SnapshotBudgetExceededError` before returning a snapshot. `copilot-exec.mjs` catches that error before `runCopilot()` and returns a distinct status, for example exit `5`, with a sentinel like `<copilot-readonly-snapshot-budget-exceeded>{...}</copilot-readonly-snapshot-budget-exceeded>`. Spill directories must be cleaned on clean runs, violation reverts, signal-triggered reverts, and budget-throw paths.

### Implementation Strategy
1. Harden nested repo discovery first. Update `findNestedRepoRoots()` to return a complete de-duplicated forest of initialized repo roots at any depth. Parent walks should stop at child repo boundaries for capture, but discovery must still descend or recurse into discovered repos to find grandchildren. Add tests for parent -> submodule -> child submodule protection without duplicate capture.
2. Introduce a nested git snapshot path in `worktree-snapshot.mjs`. Keep `captureManifest()` for non-git fallback only; remove it from initialized nested repo capture.
3. Add dirty/untracked content spill support and budget accounting. Use `lstat` before reading, reserve budget before capture, stream large spills to a temp file outside cwd, and clean spills after revert or failure. Track stats so tests can assert clean large submodules were not byte-captured.
4. Replace nested manifest revert with nested git revert. Build candidates from pre-run captured paths, post-run nested `git status --porcelain=v1 -z -uall`, and post-run index differences. Restore when worktree content/mode differs or when the index entry differs, even if bytes are unchanged. Replay nested index entries with `git update-index`.
5. Re-enable `READONLY_SNAPSHOT_ENABLED` in `copilot-exec.mjs`, add budget-exceeded handling before child spawn, and unskip the read-only guard tests.
6. Add regression fixtures for a parent repo with two initialized submodules: a large clean codex-like submodule and an ai-developer-toolkit-like target submodule with clean, dirty, staged, partially staged, staged deletion, rename, mode-bit, untracked, and binary dirty cases.
7. Bump ralph to the next version, update changelog/AGENTS release notes, update all six version stamps, and run release gates.

## Scope
### In Scope
- Per-submodule git fast-path for every initialized nested repo discovered under cwd.
- Boundary-stop and de-dup in nested repo discovery.
- Whole-cwd read-only guard preservation for initialized nested repos, including non-zone submodules.
- Exact nested worktree and index restoration for clean, dirty-unstaged, staged, partially-staged, staged deletion, rename, mode-bit, untracked, and dirty binary cases.
- Fail-closed resource budget that aborts before Copilot child launch with a distinct diagnostic.
- Re-enable the Copilot read-only snapshot/revert guard.
- Regression coverage for two initialized submodules and no-whole-tree clean submodule byte capture.
- Ralph plugin version, changelog, AGENTS, marketplace, and generated-artifact release gates.

### Out of Scope
- D-002 protected-zone scoping or policy-skipping `codex/`.
- D-004 disposable read-only lens workspace.
- A standalone hash-only detection strategy.
- Reworking parent-tree git snapshot behavior except for small reusable helper extraction.
- Restoring gitignored files inside initialized nested repos; the explicit contract is git-visible tracked and non-ignored untracked content.
- Fixing the related 0-byte-output/exit-3 robustness issue unless it falls out as a trivial diagnostic addition.
- Updating the codexu wrapper submodule pointer or `AGENTS.md` active-plugin-versions table; the lead performs that after the submodule implementation ships.

## Risk Areas
- Nested index fidelity can regress operator WIP if staged and unstaged states are not restored independently.
- Rename/copy porcelain parsing has two path tokens; both old and new paths must be candidates.
- Nested-within-nested initialized repos can be missed if discovery stops at the first `.git` boundary without recursively discovering child repo roots.
- Index-only changes can escape a byte-only comparison; nested revert must compare pre/post index entries and mode bits as first-class candidates.
- Windows path canonicalization and case-folding must remain consistent with existing zone checks.
- Spill-file cleanup must be idempotent on normal revert, clean run, error, and signal paths.
- Budget checks must never create a partial snapshot that is later treated as protective.
- Enabling the guard changes runtime behavior in `copilot-exec.mjs`; tests must prove the child is not launched on budget failure and is launched normally on clean snapshots.
- Version-stamp updates can drift across Claude/Copilot/Codex manifests and marketplace indexes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `findNestedRepoRoots()` returns each initialized nested repo once across the full nested-root forest, including a parent -> submodule -> child-submodule fixture, while parent capture skips child roots to avoid duplicate work.
- `captureSnapshot()` no longer byte-captures clean tracked files from initialized nested repos; clean nested tracked files are restored from that nested repo's HEAD/index blobs.
- Pre-existing dirty-unstaged, staged, partially-staged, staged-deletion, renamed, mode-bit changed, untracked, and dirty binary files inside an initialized nested repo are restored byte-for-byte and with index state unchanged after a child mutates them.
- Index-only and mode-only nested repo mutations are reverted even when worktree bytes are unchanged, including unstaging/restaging, resetting a partially staged file, staged add/delete, and `git update-index --chmod`.
- A child write to a clean tracked file inside an ai-developer-toolkit-like nested repo is reverted and reported as a read-only violation with exit `3`.
- A child write to a clean tracked file inside a codex-like non-zone initialized submodule is also reverted and reported, preserving whole-cwd protection.
- The large clean submodule fixture proves no whole-tree Buffer capture of clean tracked files using deterministic instrumentation: a read-spy/test hook fails if clean tracked files in the large submodule are byte-read, and snapshot stats show captured bytes/files only for dirty or untracked paths.
- When the configured budget is exceeded, `copilot-exec.mjs --read-only` emits a distinct budget diagnostic, returns a distinct non-zero status, and does not spawn the Copilot child.
- Budget accounting is stat-first: a large dirty/untracked file triggers budget failure or streaming spill without first allocating a whole Buffer in heap, and spill files are cleaned on clean, violation, signal, and budget-failure paths.
- Existing skipped read-only guard tests are re-enabled or replaced with equivalent active coverage.
- Ralph version stamps are synchronized across the three plugin manifests and the three marketplace indexes.
- The ralph test suite and release gates pass, with any documented Windows environmental failures called out only if they pre-exist the change.

## Preliminary Story Decomposition
- **US-001: Harden nested repo discovery and snapshot shape.** Build a complete de-duplicated nested-root forest, skip child roots during parent capture, and introduce a nested git snapshot data structure.
- **US-002: Restore nested repos through git metadata with dirty spill.** Replace nested manifest replay with index-aware nested revert, independent index/mode difference detection, and stat-first dirty/untracked byte spill.
- **US-003: Add fail-closed budget and no-whole-tree instrumentation.** Account for dirty/untracked capture costs, abort before child launch, expose stats, and add deterministic read-spy/test-hook assertions.
- **US-004: Re-enable Copilot read-only guard and integration tests.** Flip `READONLY_SNAPSHOT_ENABLED`, add budget handling in `copilot-exec.mjs`, and unskip/extend guard tests.
- **US-005: Update release metadata and gates.** Bump the ralph plugin version, changelog, AGENTS release notes, manifests, marketplace indexes, and verify generated artifacts.

## Suggested Decomposition
Cluster the preliminary stories for possible parallel execution. The recommended execution is serial because the high-risk stories share the same snapshot schema and restore path.

## Open Questions
- Exact budget defaults should be chosen during implementation after measuring the fixture and existing dirty-file costs. Recommended default: conservative, configurable constants with tests using small injected limits.
- Budget-exceeded exit code should be distinct from existing `3` violation and `4` revert-failed statuses. This plan recommends exit `5`, but implementation should confirm no existing caller relies on that code.
- Dirty-content spill can be all captured dirty/untracked content or only large/binary content. The plan prefers spilling large/binary content and tracking total captured bytes; tests should assert heap is not proportional to clean tracked tree size.
